items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess up to 3 ounces of cannabis and 24 g of concentrate, and use it in a private home or most places tobacco smoking is allowed, but not in vehicles, businesses, restaurants (including patios), hookah or cigar bars, federal property, or most public and state parks and beaches. 'Gifting' alongside a sale is illegal; home growing isn't yet allowed for adult use.

psychoactive-substances.notes: State or provincial law. Read with the national rules (in the US, cannabis stays illegal federally: no federal land, no crossing state lines).

laws.rule: Adults 21 and over may possess up to 3 ounces of cannabis and 24 g of concentrate, and use it in a private home or most places tobacco may be smoked, but not in vehicles (even parked), restaurants including patios, businesses, hookah or cigar bars, most public and state parks, or beaches. Taking cannabis across state lines is illegal. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land such as national parks.

New York generally prohibits possessing a handgun, short-barrelled rifle or shotgun, or assault weapon outside your home or business without a New York licence, and New York City has its own separate licensing. Out-of-state permits are not a substitute.

New York City (not the state) bans drinking alcohol in a public place, or holding an open container with the intent to drink it, except at a permitted block party, feast or similar event (Administrative Code 10-125). Since 2016 the penalty can be a civil penalty heard at the city's tribunal (OATH) instead of a criminal summons.
laws.penalty_signal: fine up to US$25 (about A$36 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: Smoking and vaping are banned in New York City parks, beaches, marinas and boardwalks, in the Parks Department's aquatic and recreation buildings, and on pedestrian plazas set up by the city's transport department (such as those in Times Square). Sidewalks beside parks are exempt. The 2011 law was extended to e-cigarettes in 2014.
laws.penalty_signal: fine of US$50 per violation (about A$71 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: In New York City the speed limit for e-bikes, e-scooters and pedal-assist bikes is 15 mph (24 km/h), even though a Class 1 or 2 e-bike can reach 20 mph and Class 3 25 mph. E-bikes may use bike lanes, park drives and greenways, and streets with limits of 30 mph or less. E-scooters may not be ridden on sidewalks. The minimum age for e-bike riders is 16, and helmets are required for Class 3 e-bikes and for e-scooter riders aged 16 and 17.

A hotel room occupancy tax applies in New York City on top of the room rate and is paid by the guest: the city percentage rate plus a flat amount per room per night (50 cents for a rent of US$10 to under US$20, US$1.00 for US$20 to under US$30, US$1.50 for US$30 to under US$40, and US$2.00 for US$40 or more; about A$2.84 at the top tier at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026). Each room of a suite counts. The percentage rate was not stated on the page read.

The Penal Law defines 'sparkling devices' as ground-based or hand-held devices whose main effect is sparks, colour or smoke, which do not rise into the air, fire projectiles or explode, and treats them separately from 'fireworks' (which cover other explosive devices and skyrockets). Check the section and local rules before buying: this entry records the definition only, not the sale and use rules in sections 270.00 to 270.05.

layers.authority: Adirondack Mountain Reserve (operator) with NYS Department of Environmental Conservation
layers.process: A free reservation is required for parking, day access and overnight access to the trails through the Adirondack Mountain Reserve gate (Keene Valley, Route 73) and to Round and Noonmark mountains, 1 May to 31 October. Walk-ins without a reservation are not permitted; people dropped off or arriving by bike also need one. Book at hikeamr.org (an account is needed). Details here are from the operator's FAQ dated 8 April 2025; the DEC announced the system's return for 2026 with bookings opening 17 April 2026, but the DEC page could not be opened by automated fetch, so the 2026 booking window and daily cap should be rechecked on hikeamr.org. The 2025 FAQ gave a two-week booking window, overnight stays of up to three nights, and lot access 5 am to 7 pm. The system does not apply to other parts of the Adirondack Park. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
